items.q: What does an AI marketing specialist for the pharmaceutical sector do?
items.a: Plans and produces marketing for pharmaceutical companies, pharmacies, drug warehouses, pharmacists and their products — campaigns, videos, websites, content and interactive experiences — using AI for speed and creativity, and pharmaceutical knowledge to keep every claim accurate and compliant.

items.q: Can you advertise prescription medicines on social media?
items.a: No. In Jordan, direct promotion of medicines to patients is prohibited and promotional material for prescription medicines goes to healthcare professionals only. For the public, I market pharmacy services, permitted products and health education — and OTC media ads go to the JFDA for prior approval.

items.q: How do you keep AI-made marketing accurate?
items.a: AI drafts; I check. Every claim is compared with the registered product information and the leaflet, nothing is published without your sign-off, and I never use fake doctors, patients or testimonials.

items.q: What does a typical campaign include?
items.a: A one-page brief, a claim check, the AI-produced pieces (posts, short videos, visuals, landing page or catalog), my pharmacist review, your approval, then launch with simple KPIs agreed at the start.

items.q: What AI qualifications do you have?
items.a: A CPD-accredited certificate from Relevancy Academy for the training “AI for Business to Increase Productivity” (15 training hours, 15–26 November 2026, certificate no. AINOVJ0453), plus ongoing structured self-study in AI foundations and hands-on work with AI assistants, prompting and agents.

items.q: What can you create with AI?
items.a: Websites and landing pages, videos and motion content, games and interactive experiences, marketing campaigns, content, documents and presentations, and small AI tools and agents — using AI throughout the process, from idea to finished product.

items.q: How do you approach data privacy and regulated data?
items.a: Collect only the data a task needs, avoid patient-identifiable data unless it is approved and protected, respect data-integrity and validation expectations in GMP and GCP environments, and keep a visible record of human decisions.
